newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile appeals court electricity price ruling.
newsitem.headline: Chile appeals court electricity price ruling.

text.p: The Chilean government will appeal to the Supreme Court over a lower court decision to reject new electricity distribution prices after complaints from power companies, said a government lawyer.
"The ruling seems surprising to me. Of course we are going to appeal the decision today to the Supreme Court so that it will be overturned," said National Energy Commission (CNE) lawyer Jaime Varela.

An appeal court had accepted unanimously Friday claims by three companies, including Chile's largest electricity distributor Chilectra, that the methods used by the CNE for fixing the new rates last year were unfair.
While the companies and government agree that prices should fall to reflect greater efficiency in the industry, the dispute is over how far they should drop.
"The ruling shows that the distribution companies' arguments are strong enough," said analyst Eleanor Lefebure of Santander Investments.
"(But) prices will be delayed further which means more uncertainty."
Chilectra appealed in October against the new distribution rates which were to have come into force in November and are due to last until 1999.

Although no official figures have been published by either side, the CNE is widely believed to want to cut prices by up to 10 percent whereas the firms argue that the reduction should be around five percent.
Power company stocks fell sharply in the run-up to Christmas over fears of a steep cut in distribution prices.
